Today's international headlines:
- Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says: The US Department of Justice says the men were involved in a string of plots, including a major incident near the UK airbase that is used by US armed forces.
- US Army soldier suspected of spying for Russia arrested in UK: The 41-year-old senior soldier is accused of national security offences and is being questioned in London.
- US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, for now: Trump welcomes the outcome, praising Hegseth as a "Great American Patriot", but Democrats can try again next year.
- Meghan's father Thomas Markle back in federal custody after allegedly removing ankle monitor: The 82-year-old was placed under house detention in Florida last week after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.
- 'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El Niño with floods predicted: Forecasters warn that this year's El Niño could be one of the strongest on record, with heavy rain and flooding in Kenya.
- Headquarters of Haitian gang destroyed, El Salvador's president says: The infamous 400 Mawozo gang was targeted by the El Salvador military which has deployed thousands of troops to combat Haiti's gang violence crisis.
- Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned: The ruling brings to an end an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones.
- Kennedys sue to block Trump's arch, arguing it would cast shadow on JFK's grave: Nine members of the political dynasty say the 250ft structure would cast a shadow on gravesites.
- Violence erupts in Bangladesh as ousted PM's supporters stage protest: Supporters of Sheikh Hasina want her to return from exile in India.
- Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government: Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has first chance to build a new government and oust the prime minister.
- Spain's king and queen attend memorial service for rail crash victims: Sixty-nine people died in the collision near Toledo two weeks ago and 28 are still in hospital.
- Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions: Najib Razak was convicted for his role in the billion-dollar scandal involving the 1MDB sovereign wealth fund.
